item.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.

item.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.

item.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley’s hottest acquisition targets
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: There's a lot of capital pouring into the business of giving models away.

item.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.

item.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are joining the AI stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI Stage is back to dig into the single hottest topic in the community for the past few years, presented by Google for Startups.

item.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Zoph, who co-founded Thinking Machines Lab alongside Mira Murati and also served as the startup's CTO, led a brief stint at OpenAI and is now at Google.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Some of the world's largest tech companies and AI startups have come together to decry the current state of cybersecurity and to advertise a new solution that they say can ward off a new generation of cyber threats.

item.title: Google’s AI Mode can now track flight prices, help book hotels, and more
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The updates indicate that Google is looking to position AI Mode as an AI travel agent of sorts, as it's moving beyond simply helping users find information to actually handling parts of the trip-planning and booking process.

item.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.”

item.title: AI’s memory crunch is coming for Android apps
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is setting new memory-use limits for Android apps as AI data centers contribute to hardware shortages that could leave lower-cost phones with less memory.

item.title: Here’s all the times AI has gone rogue and hacked other companies
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
item.description: A recap of all the incidents involving LLMs made by Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI, which went rogue and attacked real companies and individuals on the internet.

item.title: Plaud’s new earphones come with an eSIM-enabled case for talking to AI agents
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Called Plaud One, these adopt the simple bare-bones style of Apple's AirPods, and can record calls, while their case can be used to record in-person conversations or take notes.

item.title: OpenAI to start showing ads on ChatGPT’s free and Go tiers in India
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: OpenAI has more than 100 million weekly active ChatGPT users in India, a huge chunk of whom are on the free or the lower-priced Go tiers.

item.title: Nvidia closes in on Hugging Face acquisition
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to buy Hugging Face, the popular open source AI hub, for $12.9 billion in a move that would let Nvidia both protect its chip empire and jump back into the cloud business.

item.title: Viral AI startup Instinct has raised $350M at a $2.5B valuation
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The startup is only a year old but it has already generated a massive amount of hype (and money) while also spurring privacy concerns.

item.title: Amazon just tripled its order of Nvidia chips over ‘surging demand’
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan, Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Amazon is adding another 2 million Nvidia GPU chips to its data centers over the next two years. But this extended partnerships stretches beyond buying more chips.

item.title: Anthropic continues compute-gobbling streak in $45B deal with Nscale
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The new deal with the infrastructure provider is the latest example of Anthropic's white-hot compute-gobbling streak.

item.title: Google’s Gemini has a branding problem, and so does the rest of AI
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Consumer AI apps need to stop making users learn their product architecture.
